text:
Pittsburgh is a team waiting for the phone to ring. Josh Yohe, the Penguins' beat reporter, has said Erik Karlsson and Rickard Rakell are about to be traded, Sidney Crosby's contract future hangs over everything, and Wednesday's 6-3 loss to Calgary made it five straight without a win (0-5-0). Both Karlsson and Rakell had a hand in the scoring. It did not change much.

The Penguins had the better of the first period, out-chancing Calgary 1.09 to 0.32 in expected goals (the quality of chances created), and Tommy Novak gave them a 1-0 lead at 16:20. Then the Flames went to the front of the net. Joel Farabee, Brennan Othmann and Maxim Tsyplakov all scored on tip-ins in the first 10:37 of the second period, three deflections that turned a deficit into a 3-1 lead. Othmann's goal was the night's biggest swing, taking Calgary from 48% to 67% to win, and he added an assist in only 9:42 of ice time.

Pittsburgh kept answering on the power play, where it went 2 for 5. Evgeni Malkin scored on a backhand from Karlsson and Rakell, and Rakell finished a 35% look 21 seconds after Ryan Strome had restored a two-goal lead. That was as close as it got. Jonathan Castagna, the rookie whose first two NHL goals came against San Jose, added another in the third, and Yegor Sharangovich closed it at 17:41.

This is a game the Penguins could reasonably say they deserved: by shot quality they win it about 66% of the time. But Arturs Silovs let in five on 26 shots, about 2.5 more than those shots deserved, while Dustin Wolf stopped 25 of 28, including a 27% chance from Justin Brazeau in the second. For Calgary, it snapped a three-game winless run (0-2-1). For Pittsburgh, it was another night that felt like a preview of a roster about to change.
headline: Flames tip their way past a Penguins team in sell mode
